is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae, Anopheles coluzzii, Anopheles funestus, and Anopheles pharoensis (page 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L1014F (kdr-w) and L1014S (kdr-e) (page 7, page 10).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper states: 'The kdr mutations were detected in ~98% and in ~76% of A. gambiae and A. coluzzii, respectively (SI Appendix, Table S12, and Dataset S1)' (page 7). The sample size for genotyping is explicitly given as 361 (page 7).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in Bangui, Central African Republic (page 2, page 10).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study involving field collections and laboratory analysis of mosquitoes (page 2, page 10).

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were made at four specific sites in Bangui: Gbanikola, Iles des Singes, Ouango, and Pk10 (page 9, page 10).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted between June 2016 and May 2017 (page 2, page 10).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new collection effort conducted between 2016 and 2017.

supplement.evidence: The necessary genotype data is summarized in the text and referenced to SI Appendix Table S12 and Dataset S1, which are part of the provided document.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the biting behavior of Anopheles mosquitoes in Bangui, Central African Republic, through 48-hour collections. It also assessed the prevalence of kdr-w (L1014F) and kdr-e (L1014S) mutations in a subset of 361 mosquitoes.
